chapters.title: Chapter 2: How Each Component Is Taxed

children.text: Karthik, a data engineer in Hyderabad, pays ₹40,000 a month for a 2BHK in Gachibowli. He is in the old tax regime. Last year his HRA exemption was capped at 40% of his basic, because Hyderabad was treated as a non-metro. From tax year 2026-27, Hyderabad is on the 50% list, and the same salary and the same flat now give him ₹60,000 more exemption and about ₹18,720 less tax.

HRA is the biggest exemption most salaried Indians ever claim, and one of the most miscalculated. This lesson gives you the exact three-way test, shows which limit decides your number, and covers the paperwork that now comes with it.

body.text: Everything in this lesson applies only if you are in the old tax regime. In the default new regime, HRA is fully taxable no matter how much rent you pay.

children.text: The rule in one formula
Your HRA exemption, under Section 11 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 10(13A) of the 1961 Act) read with the Income-tax Rules, 2026, is the lowest of three amounts:

body.caption: 50% in the 8 listed cities, 40% everywhere else. All amounts for the same period.

children.text: Actual HRA received
: what your employer pays you as HRA for the period.
Rent paid minus 10% of salary
: the first 10% of your salary is treated as rent you would pay anyway.
50% or 40% of salary
: a cap based on where you live and work.
And "salary" here has a specific meaning.
Salary for HRA
is not your gross or your CTC. It is basic, plus DA that counts for retirement benefits, plus any commission fixed as a percentage of turnover. For most private sector employees, it is simply basic.

markDefs.definition: Basic pay plus dearness allowance if it forms part of retirement benefits, plus any commission paid as a fixed percentage of turnover. Special allowance, HRA and other allowances are not included.

body.text: Karthik's taxable income stays above ₹10,00,000 even after all his exemptions and deductions, so every extra rupee of exemption saves him tax at the old regime's 30% slab plus 4% cess: ₹60,000 × 31.2% = ₹18,720.

children.text: Which limit is holding you back?
The limit that bites changes as your rent changes. Here is Karthik's exemption at different rent levels, keeping his salary and HRA fixed.

body.title: Karthik's annual HRA exemption by monthly rent

cells: Your rent is low relative to your basic
Only higher genuine rent. Nothing to fix in your structure
Your employer pays too little HRA for your rent
Ask HR to raise HRA from special allowance, up to 50% of basic in listed cities
Your basic is low relative to your rent
A higher basic, which also raises PF and gratuity

body.title: Read the binding limit
body.question: Karthik moves to a ₹50,000 a month flat. His exemption is stuck at ₹4,20,000. Which change to his salary structure, with CTC unchanged, could increase it?
options: Raise HRA only, keeping basic the same
None, ₹4,20,000 is the legal maximum for everyone
body.explanation: At ₹50,000 rent, both actual HRA (₹4,20,000) and 50% of salary (₹4,20,000) are binding. Raising HRA alone hits the 50%-of-basic cap. Raising basic alone hits the actual HRA cap. Only raising both lifts the lowest limit, up to rent minus 10% of salary, which is ₹5,16,000.

children.text: When low rent is the limiting factor
Priyanka, a teacher at a private school in Jaipur, has basic of ₹50,000 a month and HRA of ₹20,000. She rents a modest flat for ₹12,000 a month. Jaipur is not on the 50% list, so her cap is 40%.
Rent minus 10% of salary: ₹1,44,000 minus ₹60,000 = ₹84,000
Exempt HRA: ₹84,000. Taxable HRA: ₹1,56,000

For Priyanka, the first ₹60,000 of rent a year earns her nothing, because it only covers the 10% of salary deduction. That is why HRA exemption rewards people with high rent relative to basic, and why it often matters little in smaller cities.
When rent changes mid-year

body.title: Karthik moves house in October: why you calculate period by period

children.text: The three limits are applied to the period during which you actually pay rent and receive HRA. If rent, HRA or salary changes during the year, calculate each period separately and add them up.
Karthik pays ₹40,000 a month from April to September, then moves to a ₹50,000 flat from October to March. His basic (₹70,000) and HRA (₹35,000) do not change.

If you wrongly lumped the full year together, you would get the lowest of ₹4,20,000, ₹4,56,000 and ₹4,20,000, which is ₹4,20,000. That overstates the exemption by ₹12,000, because a different limit bites in each half of the year.
Your turn

body.title: Sana in Pune
body.prompt: Sana works in Pune and is in the old regime. Basic ₹60,000 a month, HRA ₹24,000 a month, no DA, rent ₹25,000 a month for the full year. What is her annual HRA exemption?
body.explanation: Salary = ₹7,20,000. Actual HRA = ₹2,88,000. Rent minus 10% of salary = ₹3,00,000 minus ₹72,000 = ₹2,28,000. 50% of salary (Pune is now on the list) = ₹3,60,000. Lowest = ₹2,28,000.

body.title: Rohit in Mumbai
body.prompt: Rohit works in Mumbai and is in the old regime. Basic ₹1,00,000 a month, HRA ₹40,000 a month, rent ₹80,000 a month for the full year. What is his annual HRA exemption?
body.explanation: Salary = ₹12,00,000. Actual HRA = ₹4,80,000. Rent minus 10% of salary = ₹9,60,000 minus ₹1,20,000 = ₹8,40,000. 50% of salary = ₹6,00,000. Lowest = actual HRA of ₹4,80,000. Rohit's HRA component is the binding limit, so raising HRA towards 50% of basic would help him.

body.text: Rohit pays more than ₹50,000 a month in rent. That makes him responsible for deducting TDS at 2% on the rent under Section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 194-IB of the 1961 Act), which is ₹19,200 for the full year, and depositing it. This applies to individual tenants whatever their tax regime, and many people claiming HRA miss it.

children.text: Rent to parents, spouses and your own house

body.title: Who can be your landlord?
body.question: Which of these HRA claims is most likely to be rejected?
options: Paying rent by bank transfer to your mother, who owns the flat and reports the rent in her return
Paying rent to your spouse, who owns the flat you both live in
Renting a flat in Pune where you work while owning a house in Nagpur
Renting a flat from an unrelated landlord who has given you his PAN
body.explanation: Rent to a spouse for a home you share is generally not accepted as genuine, since spouses normally live together as one household. Rent to parents can work if they actually own the house, receive the money through a bank and report it as income. Owning a house in another city does not stop you claiming HRA where you work.

body.title: The rent-to-parents idea
body.scenario: Ankit, 29, lives with his retired parents in their own flat in Ahmedabad and works nearby. He is in the old regime with basic of ₹80,000 a month and HRA of ₹40,000 a month. A colleague tells him to "pay" his father ₹30,000 a month as rent and claim HRA. His father has pension income of ₹4,00,000 a year and no other income.
body.prompt: Can Ankit do this? What must be true for it to hold up, and does it actually save the family tax?
body.modelAnswer: It can be legitimate, but only if it is real. The father must own the flat, Ankit must actually transfer ₹30,000 every month from his bank account, there should be a rent agreement, and his father must report the ₹3,60,000 as rental income in his own return. Ankit must now also disclose his relationship with the landlord in Form 124. Ankit's exemption: salary ₹9,60,000, actual HRA ₹4,80,000, rent minus 10% of salary ₹2,64,000, 50% of salary ₹4,80,000, so ₹2,64,000 exempt. His father's taxable rent is ₹3,60,000 minus the 30% standard deduction on house property, which is ₹2,52,000, added to his pension. Whether the family saves depends on the father's regime and slab, but with modest income he is likely to pay far less on it than Ankit saves at 30%. What does not work: receipts without actual payments, cash rent, or the father not reporting the income. The department can match Ankit's claim with his father's return.

children.text: The paperwork, from 1 April 2026

body.title: Before you submit your HRA claim
steps: Sign a rent agreement with your landlord
Pay rent through bank transfer, UPI or cheque, not cash
Get your landlord's PAN if annual rent is more than ₹1,00,000
Declare rent, landlord details and your relationship with the landlord in Form 124
Deduct and deposit 2% TDS if your rent is more than ₹50,000 a month
Recalculate by period if your rent, basic or HRA changed during the year

body.title: The new form
body.textWithBlank: From tax year 2026-27, employees declare rent and other tax-saving claims to their employer in Form ___, which replaces Form 12BB.
body.explanation: Form 124 under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 replaces Form 12BB. The notable addition for HRA is that you must now disclose your relationship with the landlord.

body.text: Fake rent receipts are a classic mistake. The Annual Information Statement, landlord PAN disclosure and your landlord's own return give the tax department several ways to match your claim. A disallowed claim means extra tax, interest and possible penalties.

No HRA in your salary at all, but paying rent? In the old regime, you may be able to claim a separate deduction for rent paid (Section 80GG of the 1961 Act), capped at ₹5,000 a month and subject to conditions. It is not available in the new regime.

Figures use tax year 2026-27 rules under the old tax regime. HRA claims have further conditions around genuine residence and documentation. This lesson is for education and is not personalised tax advice.

points: HRA exemption exists only in the old regime and equals the lowest of actual HRA, rent minus 10% of salary, and 50% or 40% of salary.
Salary for HRA means basic plus retirement-linked DA plus turnover-based commission, not gross pay.
From tax year 2026-27, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad join Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata and Chennai at the 50% cap.
Find your binding limit: low rent, low HRA or low basic each need a different fix.
Calculate period by period when rent, HRA or basic changes during the year.
Form 124 replaces Form 12BB and now requires disclosure of your relationship with the landlord. Rent above ₹50,000 a month requires 2% TDS.
